---
title: Limits
---

Sentinel is one layer of oversight.
It works with your agent's sandbox, permission settings, and approvals, and it does not replace them.

## Some commands get past Sentinel, so keep your sandbox on

Sentinel reads the text of each command before it runs.
It does not run the command or watch what the command does.
A command whose effect is not visible in its text can therefore get past Sentinel.
For example:

- a program given to an interpreter, such as `uv run python -c 'print(open(".env").read())'`
- a file name kept in a variable, such as `f=.env; cat "$f"`
- a command inside `bash -c` or `eval`
- a symbolic link that points to a secret
- a recursive search of a directory that holds a secret, such as `grep -r token ~`

Set your agent's sandbox to deny reads of your credential files, and limit its network access.
Then a command that gets past Sentinel still cannot read those files or send them off your computer.

## Agent configuration options can remove the protection Sentinel depends on

Sentinel depends on your agent's sandbox and permission settings.
Unwise configuration settings can turn them off for a whole session, for example the Claude Code `bypassPermissions` mode or the Codex `danger-full-access` sandbox mode.
Sentinel cannot detect that this has happened.
The [session-start report](session-start-report.qmd) warns about settings that turn Sentinel's hooks off, but it does not check sandbox, network, or permission settings.

**Do not use a mode that bypasses your agent's permissions or sandbox.**

## Agents may enforce the same policy differently

Sentinel applies one policy in every agent, but the agents give Sentinel different ways to enforce it.
Where an agent cannot do what the policy requires, Sentinel handles the failure in the safe direction.
For example:

- Codex cannot show you a question, so Sentinel refuses each action it would otherwise ask you about.
  You will see more refusals in Codex than in other agents.
- Copilot CLI cannot show a question in a session started with `-p` or in autopilot mode, so it refuses those actions.
- In Copilot CLI's assisted mode, a model can answer Sentinel's questions for you.
  Sentinel cannot prevent this, and the session-start report warns when your settings allow it.

If your work often needs actions that Sentinel asks about, use an agent that can show you the question.

## Some controls are outside what Sentinel can check

- GitHub can deliver Copilot policy from its servers.
  Sentinel reads only the settings files on your computer, so it cannot report a server-delivered policy that turns hooks off.
  Ask your administrator what policy applies to your account.
- A Claude Code mod can approve an action that a Sentinel hook refused.
  Install only mods that you trust.
